[FACT] User inquired about how referees use technology during a game and FIBA Europe's regulation of this use.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Referees use technology to get a better understanding of game situations, including video replay systems, instant replay, and communication devices.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] FIBA Europe regulates the use of technology by providing guidelines and ensuring referees are trained on how to use the tools effectively.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] FIBA Europe determines when and how technology can be used during a game to ensure fairness and accuracy.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Referees typically use technology a few times during a game to review plays.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The criteria for reviewing plays varies across different basketball leagues and governing bodies.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] In FIBA Europe competitions, referees can review specific incidents such as basket interference, buzzer-beater shots, and fouls at the end of quarters or overtimes.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Video replay can slow the game down, but systems are in place to minimize delays.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] In some leagues, referees communicate with officials in the replay center for quick decisions without stopping the game.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] There are time limits for reviewing plays in some leagues; for example, in the NBA, reviews must be completed within 90 seconds, and in EuroLeague games, within 60 seconds.  
[USER] Asked how often referees use technology during a game and how it affects the pace of the game, as well as if there is a time limit for reviewing plays.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Some people argue that technology takes away from the human aspect of the game and may weaken referees' decision-making skills.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Others argue that technology helps referees make more accurate and fair decisions, especially in controversial situations.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The use of technology is about finding a balance between fair decisions and maintaining the human aspect of the game.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Opinions on the use of technology by referees differ among players, coaches, officials, and fans.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] The goal is to enhance the game's integrity while preserving its human and unpredictable aspects.
